The signature Himalayan journey

Everest Base Camp
Trek — 14 Days

Walk in the footsteps of legends, through Sherpa villages and beneath the world's highest peaks. Fourteen thoughtfully paced days, a local team who feels like family, and a moment at base camp you'll carry forever.

01 / The extraordinary moments

More than a destination.

The big views are only the beginning. It's the little moments along the way that make this journey yours.

Walk among giants

  • Stand at Everest Base Camp, 5,364 m above the everyday.
  • Catch the first light from Kala Patthar's panoramic viewpoint.

A local connection

  • Follow the trail with experienced, locally based guides.
  • Discover Sherpa hospitality and Tengboche's living traditions.

A considered pace

  • Two acclimatisation days, with time to breathe it all in.
  • Intimate groups, welcoming teahouses, and a lighter footprint.
02 / The experience

A trail to something extraordinary.

Some places ask you to slow down. The Khumbu is one of them. From the first flight into Lukla, you'll follow the Dudh Koshi through pine forests, cross prayer-flag-draped bridges, and arrive in villages where mountain life moves to its own rhythm.

Beyond Namche Bazaar, the landscape opens into a world of stone, sky, and snow. Ama Dablam watches over the trail. Monastery bells carry on the wind. And, step by steady step, the Khumbu Glacier leads you to the foot of Everest.

This is a trek, not a technical climb. The challenge is the altitude and the long walking days. Our route makes space for acclimatisation, with a local guide, porter support, and the simple comfort of a warm teahouse at day's end.

“The best part isn't reaching the end. It's who you become along the way.”

05 / The story, day by day

Every step has its own magic.

Unfold each day for the details, the practicalities, and a little inspiration. Walking times are approximate; your guide adapts the pace to the group and conditions.

01

Day 1: Arrive in KathmanduA warm welcome. The adventure begins.
Altitude
1,400 m
Trek duration
Arrival day
Accommodation
Boutique hotel
Meals
Welcome dinner

Namaste, and welcome to Nepal. Your airport transfer brings you to a characterful hotel in Kathmandu, with time to settle in and wander the lanes of Thamel. In the afternoon, meet your guide and fellow travellers for a relaxed trip briefing and an equipment check.

Over a welcome dinner, we'll talk through the trail, mountain etiquette, and what to expect at altitude. Your guide will confirm tomorrow's flight arrangements, which may include an early drive to Ramechhap during busy trekking seasons.

02

Day 2: Fly to Lukla & trek to PhakdingInto the mountains, and onto the trail.
Altitude
2,610 m · Lukla 2,860 m
Trek duration
3–4 hours walking
Accommodation
Teahouse
Meals
Breakfast, lunch & dinner

A weather-dependent mountain flight takes us to Lukla, where we meet the porter team and set off on our first gentle trail. Descending through small settlements, we follow stone paths and cross our first suspension bridges above the Dudh Koshi.

Phakding is a lovely place to find your walking rhythm. Settle into the teahouse, enjoy a hot meal, and listen to the river as the day draws to a close. Flight departure points and timings will be confirmed locally.

03

Day 3: Phakding to Namche BazaarRiver crossings and a first glimpse of Everest.
Altitude
3,440 m
Trek duration
6–7 hours walking
Accommodation
Teahouse
Meals
Breakfast, lunch & dinner

The trail follows the river through pine forests and villages before entering Sagarmatha National Park. After the high suspension bridge, we begin the sustained climb towards Namche. With clear weather, Everest may make its first appearance through the trees.

Namche Bazaar rises in a natural amphitheatre of colourful roofs. It's the Sherpa heart of the Khumbu, and our home for two nights. We'll walk slowly, take generous breaks, and arrive with time for a warm meal and an early rest.

04

Day 4: Acclimatise in Namche BazaarClimb a little higher. Sleep a little lower.
Altitude
3,440 m · hike to 3,880 m
Trek duration
3–4 hours walking
Accommodation
Teahouse
Meals
Breakfast, lunch & dinner

Today is about adjustment, not distance. A measured morning hike towards the Everest View area gives us an opportunity to walk higher before returning to Namche to sleep. On a clear day, Everest, Lhotse, and Ama Dablam form an unforgettable skyline.

The afternoon is yours to explore local shops, learn about Sherpa mountain life, or simply read with a cup of tea. Your guide checks how everyone is feeling and helps you keep the day gentle. Acclimatisation is a vital part of the journey, not an optional extra.

05

Day 5: Namche Bazaar to TengbocheMountain panoramas and monastery bells.
Altitude
3,860 m
Trek duration
5–6 hours walking
Accommodation
Teahouse
Meals
Breakfast, lunch & dinner

We contour along the hillside with wide views of Ama Dablam, then descend to the river for lunch. A steady climb through rhododendron and conifer woodland leads to Tengboche, set on a ridge with a remarkable mountain backdrop.

If the monastery is open to visitors, we'll enter respectfully and quietly, following local guidance. The evening light across the surrounding peaks is reason enough to linger outside before returning to the warmth of our teahouse.

06

Day 6: Tengboche to DingbocheWhere the trees give way to open sky.
Altitude
4,410 m
Trek duration
5–6 hours walking
Accommodation
Teahouse
Meals
Breakfast, lunch & dinner

After descending through Deboche, we cross the river and continue towards Pangboche, passing stone walls and small fields. The trees slowly thin, the valley broadens, and Ama Dablam offers a different face with every turn of the trail.

Our destination is Dingboche, an open, sunlit village ringed by high peaks. The air is thinner now, so the pace stays deliberate. Two nights here give us another important opportunity to adjust before moving into the upper Khumbu.

07

Day 7: Acclimatise in DingbocheA steady climb, and space to breathe.
Altitude
4,410 m · optional hike higher
Trek duration
4–5 hours walking
Accommodation
Teahouse
Meals
Breakfast, lunch & dinner

We take a gradual acclimatisation walk on the ridge above Dingboche, with views towards Makalu and the Imja Valley when skies are clear. How high we go depends on the group and the conditions; the Nangkartshang viewpoint is an option, not a target to push through symptoms for.

Back in the village, spend the afternoon resting, eating well, and keeping an eye on how you feel. This second acclimatisation day helps us prepare for the next stages, though it can't eliminate the risk of altitude illness.

08

Day 8: Dingboche to LobucheInto the high, quiet world of the Khumbu.
Altitude
4,910 m
Trek duration
5–6 hours walking
Accommodation
Teahouse
Meals
Breakfast, lunch & dinner

A broad trail leads across the valley towards Dughla. We climb slowly to the memorial ridge, a moving place to pause and reflect on the mountains and those who have loved them. Please be respectful of the memorials and the people visiting them.

Beyond the ridge, the landscape becomes spare and powerful, with the glacier beside us and the high peaks drawing closer. We reach Lobuche, eat a hearty meal, and settle in early for tomorrow's longer day.

09

Day 9: Gorak Shep & Everest Base CampThe moment you came for. The memories you keep.
Altitude
5,164 m · base camp 5,364 m
Trek duration
7–8 hours walking
Accommodation
Basic teahouse
Meals
Breakfast, lunch & dinner

We follow the rocky trail beside the Khumbu Glacier to Gorak Shep, where we leave our overnight bags and pause for food. Then comes the final stretch to Everest Base Camp, across glacial moraine with Nuptse rising dramatically above us.

At approximately 5,364 metres, take a breath, share the moment, and let the scale of the place sink in. Expedition tents are seasonal, and Everest's summit itself is not clearly visible from base camp. We return to Gorak Shep for a well-earned rest; reaching camp depends on health and conditions.

10

Day 10: Kala Patthar & descend to PhericheFirst light on the giants. Then homeward.
Altitude
5,545 m high · sleep 4,240 m

7–8 hours walking
Accommodation

Meals

If weather and wellbeing allow, an early start takes us up Kala Patthar for panoramic views of Everest and its neighbours. The climb is optional: an extra hour of rest is the right choice if your guide advises it or you aren't feeling well.

After breakfast, we begin our descent, retracing the high valley before turning towards Pheriche. As we lose altitude, the walking becomes more comfortable, but the long day still calls for a steady pace and frequent breaks.

11

Day 11: Pheriche to Namche BazaarFamiliar paths, seen with new eyes.
Altitude

Accommodation

Breakfast, lunch & dinner

We descend through Pangboche and return to the greener slopes around Tengboche. The day's trail includes both descents and climbs, but the thicker air and returning forests bring a welcome change of rhythm.

Back in Namche, there's time for a bakery treat or a slow wander through the village. The mountains are still with us, but the perspective is different now. Gather over dinner and trade the little stories that made the upper trail unforgettable.

12

Altitude

We take the steep descent from Namche carefully, then follow the river through villages and across suspension bridges. The final rise into Lukla is a reminder that the Himalayas rarely offer a completely flat day.

This is our last night on the trail. Share a final mountain dinner with the team and thank the people who have helped carry the journey. Your guide will explain the following morning's flight plans and any weather-related adjustments.

A morning flight, weather permitting, brings us out of Lukla. Depending on the flight schedule, we may arrive in Kathmandu directly or land in Ramechhap and continue by road. After returning to the hotel, the afternoon is free to rest or explore.

Tonight we share a farewell dinner and celebrate the journey. Keep buffer days beyond this itinerary in case mountain weather delays our return; don't schedule an international flight immediately after this planned arrival.

The trek ends, but some journeys never really leave you. Take the memories home, leave the trail as you found it, and keep a little room in your life for the extraordinary.

07 / Before you go

Prepared well. Travel beautifully.

A little preparation makes a world of difference. Here's what to know before you lace up your boots.

Fitness & experience

Expect uneven trails and several 6–8-hour days with a light daypack. Technical climbing skills aren't needed, but regular hill walking and endurance training are important. Start preparing 8–12 weeks ahead and discuss your suitability with a clinician if you have health concerns.

Seasons & flexibility

March–May brings spring trails; September–November often brings clearer skies. Weather remains unpredictable in any season. Keep at least two extra days after the trek before your international flight to allow for Lukla flight delays.

Stays & mountain meals

Kathmandu offers boutique comfort; the trail offers simple, welcoming teahouses. Rooms are usually twin-share, with shared bathrooms at higher elevations. Expect hearty dal bhat, soups, noodles, and eggs. Tell us about dietary needs before travel; options narrow with altitude.

Documents & insurance

Check Nepal's current visa and passport requirements before departure. Trek permits are included. Arrange a policy explicitly covering trekking to at least 5,545 m, search and rescue, and helicopter evacuation. Ask your insurer to confirm the coverage in writing.

The mountain sets the pace.

Altitude illness can affect anyone, regardless of fitness. Acclimatisation days reduce risk but don't eliminate it. Tell your guide about symptoms immediately, never ascend with worsening symptoms, and be prepared to descend or change the route. Your wellbeing always comes before the itinerary.

09 / Pack for the extraordinary

A lighter bag. A better journey.

Bring the essentials, leave room for the memories. Four simple checklists to get you trail-ready.

01 / Wear

The right layers

  • Moisture-wicking base layers
  • Fleece & warm down jacket
  • Waterproof shell & trousers
  • Warm hat, sun hat & gloves
  • 3–4 pairs of trekking socks
02 / Walk

Trail essentials

  • Broken-in trekking boots
  • 25–35 L daypack & rain cover
  • Adjustable trekking poles
  • 2–3 L water capacity & purification
  • UV-protective sunglasses
03 / Rest

Comfort & recovery

  • −20°C sleeping bag (loan available)
  • Lightweight lodge shoes
  • Earplugs & an eye mask
  • Personal medication & first aid
  • Compact quick-dry towel
04 / Remember

The little things

  • Passport & insurance copies
  • SPF 50 & protective lip balm
  • Headtorch & spare batteries
  • Power bank & plug adapter
  • Biodegradable toiletries

Tread lightly. Pack thoughtfully. Your porter carries up to 10 kg per guest. Airline baggage allowances are confirmed before travel; keep valuables and medication in your daypack.

10 / A little peace of mind

Good questions. Honest answers.

A big adventure should never come with little uncertainties.

Do I need previous high-altitude trekking experience?

It's helpful, but not essential. You should be comfortable walking for several hours on consecutive days, including sustained uphill sections. Fitness is only part of the picture: the itinerary includes two acclimatisation days, and your guide will adapt the pace. This trek doesn't involve ropes, ice axes, or technical climbing.

Is this a climb to the summit of Everest?

No. This journey reaches Everest Base Camp at approximately 5,364 m, not Everest's summit. The optional early-morning hike to Kala Patthar reaches around 5,545 m for panoramic mountain views. It's a demanding walking adventure, entirely separate from a mountaineering expedition.

Can I join as a solo traveller?

Absolutely. Small groups are a wonderful way to share the trail without losing your own space. The starting price assumes twin-share accommodation; a room with another solo traveller can be requested, subject to availability. Ask about a single supplement if you'd prefer your own room, noting that private rooms can't always be guaranteed in high-altitude teahouses.

What happens if I develop altitude symptoms?

Tell your guide immediately, even if symptoms seem mild. The team will stop further ascent, assess the situation, and arrange descent or medical support when appropriate. The route may change, and reaching base camp is never guaranteed. You must have suitable travel insurance for high-altitude trekking and emergency evacuation.

What if weather delays the flight to or from Lukla?

Mountain flights are weather-dependent and delays are possible. Your team will review alternatives with you, which may involve changing the programme or, if available and agreed, a helicopter at additional cost. Leave at least two buffer days after the trek before an international flight. Flight routing may use Ramechhap, requiring an early road transfer.

Will I have hot showers, Wi-Fi, and charging on the trail?

Often, but not reliably everywhere. These services usually cost extra and become more limited as you climb. Higher lodges have simple rooms and shared bathrooms. Bring a power bank, manage your expectations, and take the opportunity to disconnect a little. Your guide will advise on drinking water and local facilities each day.

How do booking, deposits, and cancellation work?

Choose a departure and complete the form to prepare your trip request. This standalone preview doesn't send your details, collect a deposit, or reserve a place. For a live booking, the operator must first confirm availability, the final price, payment instructions, and written cancellation terms. Don't make non-refundable travel arrangements before receiving that confirmation.
